summary: nolimit-agent ships heavily obfuscated bulk-email/SMS spam and OAuth-mailbox harvesting toolkit
details: Package `nolimit-agent` ships approximately 50 heavily obfuscated JavaScript modules under `.ad/` (obfuscator.io with rotated string arrays, `_0x`-mangled identifiers, RC4-decoded string literals, and a self-defending anti-prettify regex trap). The npm `main` and `bin` entry `.ad/x0.js` triggers this code on load. `package.json` describes the project as an `Advanced email sender` with keywords including `red-team,smtp`. Reachable modules implement: bulk SMS delivery via SMS-to-email carrier gateways and Twilio/Nexmo/Bandwidth APIs (`.ad/sms-providers.js`); Microsoft 365 and Google OAuth device-code flow harvesting requesting `Mail.Read Contacts.Read People.Read offline_access` and paging `/v1.0/me/mailFolders/inbox/messages?$top=250&$select=from,toRecipients,ccRecipients` for contact scraping (`.ad/x12.js`); IMAP contact extraction; DKIM keypair generation with SPF/DKIM DNS record printout for arbitrary domains; SOCKS proxy loading (`.ad/socks-loader.js`); SMTP health caching (`.ad/smtp-health-cache.js`); phone-number validation (`.ad/phone-validator.js`); and an obfuscated license-check that POSTs `{key,hwid,hostname,platform}` to a license server URL hidden inside an RC4 string table (`.ad/x4.js`, `.ad/x0.js`). Whole-code-surface self-defending obfuscation of an offensive-operations toolkit is not neutral packaging — it is a deliberate barrier to reviewer inspection of code designed to abuse third-party mail providers, SMS carriers, and OAuth-consented mailboxes. The included AUTHORIZED_USE.md disclaimer does not alter what the code does when executed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
